overclaims.statement: Arvind Krishna is senior vice president and director, IBM Research.
overclaims.citedQuote: Arvind Krishna is senior vice president and director, IBM Research.
overclaims.rationale: The ITIF bio passage describes Krishna as SVP and director of IBM Research, a role he held before becoming CEO in April 2020. Stating it in the present tense ('is') presents a past role as current; multiple other sources in the dossier confirm he is now Chairman, President and CEO.

overclaims.statement: In this role, he helps guide the company’s overall technical strategy, leading a global organization of approximately 3,000 scientists and technologists located at 12 labs on six continents.
overclaims.citedQuote: In this role, he helps guide the company’s overall technical strategy, leading a global organization of approximately 3,000 scientists and technologists located at 12 labs on six continents.
overclaims.rationale: This describes the IBM Research leadership role he held before becoming CEO; presenting it as his current role ('In this role, he...') treats a past position as present. The scale (3,000 scientists, 12 labs) is supported by the passage but only for the former role.

The 2018 WRAL/New York Times passage describes Krishna as an IBM senior vice president in charge of hybrid cloud offerings, which was his role at the time of the Red Hat announcement. The dossier statement presents this as his role without dating it, implying it is current when he has been CEO since 2020.

overclaims.statement: Senior vice president for Cloud and Cognitive Software
overclaims.citedQuote: IBM senior vice president for Cloud and Cognitive Software Arvind Krishna
overclaims.rationale: The TechCrunch passage is from January 2020, when Krishna was SVP for Cloud and Cognitive Software prior to becoming CEO in April 2020. The dossier statement lists this role without indicating it is former, implying currency.

overclaims.statement: Arvind Krishna, senior vice president for cloud and cognitive software at IBM, said IBM and Red Hat together will be in a better position to address what he described as Chapter Two of a continuing cloud journey.
overclaims.citedQuote: Arvind Krishna, senior vice president for cloud and cognitive software at IBM, said IBM and Red Hat together will be in a better position to address what he described as Chapter Two of a continuing cloud journey.
overclaims.rationale: The devops.com passage is from July 2019 when Krishna was SVP for cloud and cognitive software. The dossier statement presents this title without a date, which could imply it is his current title; he has been CEO since April 2020. The quote itself is accurately attributed, so this is a currency issue rather than a misattribution.

overclaims.statement: drove the massive $34 billion acquisition of Red Hat at the end of 2018
overclaims.citedQuote: Krishna reportedly drove the massive $34 billion acquisition of Red Hat at the end of 2018
overclaims.rationale: The TechCrunch passage says Krishna 'reportedly drove' the acquisition, hedging the claim. The dossier statement drops the 'reportedly' qualifier, asserting as fact what the source presents as a report. Other sources do support a central role, but this specific statement overstates its own citation.

overclaims.statement: He stated he could see 50% of call centre jobs going away over time
overclaims.citedQuote: The call centre jobs, I could easily see 50% of them going away over time.
overclaims.rationale: The Financial Express passage quotes Krishna saying 'The call centre jobs, I could easily see 50% of them going away over time.' The dossier's paraphrase is close, but the quote as excerpted lacks the surrounding context (which jobs, over what timeframe, in what interview); the dossier attributes a specific forward-looking claim to a snippet that alone does not establish the interview context or the full scope of his remarks. This is a mild overreach on the cited snippet alone.

overclaims.statement: He gave an interview with Bloomberg about AI job vulnerability
overclaims.citedQuote: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna in an interview with Bloomberg told about which jobs are most vulnerable to artificial intelligence
overclaims.rationale: The Financial Express passage says 'IBM CEO Arvind Krishna in an interview with Bloomberg told about which jobs are most vulnerable to artificial intelligence.' The dossier converts this into a specific claim that 'He gave an interview with Bloomberg about AI job vulnerability' — this is essentially the same content, but the dossier presents it as an independently verified fact when the citation is a secondary outlet's characterization of the interview. Borderline; the passage does support that he spoke to Bloomberg about AI and jobs.

overclaims.statement: CEO of IBM; Director of IBM Research
overclaims.citedQuote: CEO of IBM; Director of IBM Research
overclaims.rationale: The IIT Kanpur people list passage pairs 'CEO of IBM' with 'Director of IBM Research' as descriptors. Krishna headed IBM Research before becoming CEO in 2020; presenting both as simultaneous current titles treats a past role as current. The list entry likely reflects an outdated or compressed description.

overclaims.citedQuote: Arvind previously was senior vice president of Cloud and Cognitive Software, where he pioneered the company’s hybrid cloud business, transformed IBM’s entire software and services portfolio and offerings for cloud, and grew the business.
overclaims.rationale: The IBM history page passage describes Krishna's role as SVP of Cloud and Cognitive Software using past-tense framing ('Arvind previously was senior vice president'), but the dossier statement is a bare 'statement' with no temporal marker, and the claim is filed under 'career' without effectiveFrom. As extracted, it does not convey that this is a former role, risking it being read as current. Uncertain because the underlying passage itself uses 'previously,' so the source is not overstating — the risk is in the dossier's undated presentation.

usefulness.rationale: The dossier clearly establishes who Arvind Krishna is (IBM Chairman, President and CEO since April 2020, chairman since January 2021) and what he has done: led the $34B Red Hat acquisition, headed IBM Research and Cloud & Cognitive Software, founded IBM's security software business, co-authored 15 patents, and is recognized on TIME's 2026 TIME100 AI list. Career progression, education (IIT Kanpur 1985, University of Illinois PhD 1991), board roles (Northrop Grumman, NY Fed), and current strategic positions on AI, hybrid cloud, and quantum are all well covered. The dossier does not explicitly flag gaps (e.g., no family/personal-life detail, no full list of patents, no detail on compensation beyond one phantom stock grant), so it slightly implies completeness. A reader could readily prepare for a meeting: role, tenure, priorities (AI-first, hybrid cloud, quantum, consulting), leadership principles, and recent controversies (stock plunge, layoffs, meeting-phone stance) are all present. One caveat: several claims are marked 'contested' and some stale roles (SVP of IBM Research) appear alongside current ones, but the overall picture is coherent and current.
